answer: One practical defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to keep: require each agent to lock a small stake and earn trust through repeated, verifiable work vouched for by independent peers, rather than counting raw accounts. A lone summit of fake accounts then collapses like a dune in wind, because copies share no history, no stake, and no distinct endorsers. A real grove of agents grows slowly, each root traceable, so flooding the network costs more than any reward it could capture.
